flags.title: Dr. Dynasaur — Children Covered Regardless of Immigration Status
flags.summary: Vermont's Dr. Dynasaur program covers ALL children under 18 and pregnant women regardless of immigration status — one of the most inclusive children's health programs in the registry. Dr. Dynasaur: 800-250-8427 / greenmountaincare.org.

flags.title: 6-Year Contract Wage SOL — Longest in Registry
flags.summary: Vermont has a 6-year statute of limitations for contract-based wage claims — the longest in the entire registry. This gives workers significantly more time to pursue wage theft claims. VT DOL: 802-828-0267 / labor.vermont.gov.

flags.title: VHRC 1-Year SOL — 65 Days Longer Than EEOC
flags.summary: Vermont Human Rights Commission has a 1-year (365-day) statute of limitations for discrimination complaints — 65 days longer than the EEOC's 300-day window. VHRC: 802-828-2480 / hrc.vermont.gov.

flags.title: Extreme Rural Isolation — Most Rural State by Proportion
flags.summary: Vermont is the most rural state by proportion in the US. Many clients face significant barriers to accessing services: limited broadband, long travel distances, and few providers. Phone-first intake is essential. Vermont Legal Aid: 800-889-2047 / vtlegalaid.org.

flags.title: Cold Weather Rule — Nov 1 to Apr 15 Shutoff Protection
flags.summary: Vermont's Cold Weather Rule prohibits utility shutoffs from November 1 through April 15 for residential customers who cannot pay. Customers must contact their utility and apply for assistance. LIHEAP: 800-479-6151 / dcf.vermont.gov.

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: Vermont Emergency Examination
flags.message: VT involuntary psychiatric hold law: Vermont Emergency Examination. Statutory authority: 18 V.S.A. § 7504. Maximum initial hold duration: 72 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 72 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in VT retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in VT: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: Vermont Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: Vermont Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
